not-mutated.reason: Throws on missing/invalid frontmatter, but no mutated gate consumes it: wiki-ingest.ts implements its own local parseFrontmatterDocument/renderFrontmatterDocument instead of importing this module. Its one production consumer is repo-page-move.ts (itself not-mutated, below), which imports parseFrontmatterDocument/renderFrontmatterDocument; the page-move tests reach it through the built dist, not a same-tree import. wiki-write-core.test.ts additionally exercises reconstructFrontmatter, and only its happy path.

validateRenderingPolicy returns unsafe-html findings but no production gate consumes it (only wiki-write-core.test.ts calls it directly). maskCodeContent/maskNonProseContent, the functions the corrections-survival.ts gate does call, are pure content transforms with no rejection path of their own.

splitFrontmatter's error field is the only rejection-shaped output here, and its sole consumer is wiki-lint.ts, itself not-mutated pending relocation. collectWikiPages/collectWikilinks, consumed by the mutated corrections-survival.ts and wiki-ingest.ts, are non-rejecting collection helpers, and findWikilinkSpans (consumed by repo-page-move.ts, itself not-mutated) is the same scan with offsets.
resolveMarkdownLinks' exists signal is consumed only by wiki-lint.ts, itself not-mutated pending relocation; no mutated module reaches this file.

Pure locator for fenced code blocks and inline code spans, with no rejection path of its own: it returns offsets and never throws. Its consumers (markdown-links.ts and wiki-utils.ts) are themselves not-mutated, and their tests reach it through the built dist rather than a same-tree import. Pinned behaviorally by scripts/markdown-links.test.ts and scripts/wiki-utils.test.ts.

Pure re-export barrel with no logic of its own. The core logic lives in the modules it re-exports (corrections.ts, frontmatter.ts, gate-contract.ts, private-leak-adapter.ts, private-leak.ts, rendering-policy.ts, wiki-ingest.ts, wiki-lint.ts), each separately dispositioned in this list or stryker.config.json's mutate set.

Build-time constants only (version + source-tree hash placeholder), no logic to mutate. The module that carries the real check is scripts/build-wiki-write-core.ts (already in mutate), which populates and verifies GATE_SOURCE_TREE_HASH.
Its real tests are scripts/wiki-lint.test.ts, reaching it through the built dist/ output rather than a same-tree source import. Relocating those tests beside this module flips this entry to mutate.

Has a real rejection path (WikiIngestError on INVALID_PAYLOAD/INVALID_FRONTMATTER/INVALID_WIKILINK/CORRECTION_ERODED/PROTECTED_BRANCH) a gate depends on, but its real test is scripts/wiki-ingest.test.ts, which imports the built dist/ output through the scripts/wiki-ingest.ts re-export shell (`export * from '@fro.bot/wiki-write-core/wiki-ingest'`) rather than this source file. A live check:mutation-guards run confirmed 1474/1474 mutants NoCoverage under same-tree pairing. Relocating scripts/wiki-ingest.test.ts beside this module flips this entry to mutate.

Has a real rejection path (computeRepoSlug throws on an empty sanitized segment) a gate depends on, but its real test is scripts/wiki-slug.test.ts, which imports the built dist/ output through the scripts/wiki-slug.ts re-export shell (`export * from '@fro.bot/wiki-write-core/wiki-slug'`) rather than this source file. A live check:mutation-guards run confirmed only partial coverage attributable to private-leak-adapter.test.ts's direct import, not this dedicated test. Relocating scripts/wiki-slug.test.ts beside this module flips this entry to mutate.

Has a real rejection path (assertReposFile throws SchemaValidationError) a gate depends on, but its real test is scripts/schemas.test.ts, which imports the module through the @fro.bot/wiki-write-core/schemas package name rather than this source file, so a mutation run would score only the indirect exercise from private-leak-adapter.test.ts. Relocating scripts/schemas.test.ts beside this module flips this entry to mutate.

Has real rejection paths (every RepoPageMoveBlockReason: slug and private-name collisions, an unattributed or occupied page, unparseable pages, invalid index or wikilinks) that decide whether the operator rename may delete and recreate a wiki page. Its real test is packages/privacy/src/repo-page-move.test.ts, which imports the built dist/ output through the @fro.bot/wiki-write-core root barrel rather than this source file, so a same-tree mutation run would score every mutant NoCoverage. The decision table is pinned there instead: one test per block reason and per outcome. Relocating that test beside this module flips this entry to mutate.

Operator-dispatched writer, never run on a schedule: it commits to data only after a human dispatches it and GitHub itself proves the rename (same node ID, same owner, public). It does have real rejection paths (every evidence and row block, the branch and tip-author checks, a truncated tree, the path and no-overwrite policy, the 3-attempt retry), and each is pinned by a decision-table test in packages/registry/src/rename-tracked-repo.test.ts against an in-memory Git Data fake that enforces fast-forward updates. The page-move decisions it delegates to live in packages/wiki-write-core/src/repo-page-move.ts, classified separately. It is not in the mutate list because the module's boundary is its injected clients rather than a pure predicate, so a Stryker run would mostly score transport glue. Re-evaluate if it gains an unattended caller.

The one branch-safety rule shared by commit-metadata.ts, wiki-ingest.ts and rename-tracked-repo.ts (never main; never a protected branch except the canonical fro-bot/.github@data). It has a real rejection path, so it is pinned by a truth table in scripts/branch-safety.test.ts (both protection flags, every one-field deviation from the canonical target, the main short-circuit, and lookup failure propagating), and each consumer's suite pins its own refusal shape. It is not in the mutate list because its tests import it through the built dist, as repo-page-move.ts's do. Re-evaluate if the rule gains another exemption.
Pure normalization helper (whitespace collapse) with no rejection path of its own; consumed by the already-mutated corrections-survival.ts gate.
GitHub API infra-recovery helper (branch existence check/restore). Its throw paths are network/API failure handling, not content-validation logic a gate depends on.
A directive scanner cannot describe its own grammar in comments without matching it; the classifier and scanner are covered by their fixture tests, not by mutation.

Exported request-time GitHub adapter with no current CI or autonomous-write caller in this repository; only its dedicated tests and the package barrel reference it. Active privacy workflows use scripts/check-private-leak.ts and private-leak.ts directly. Re-promote when a production caller lands. Its test stays in stryker.config.json testFiles regardless: it is private-leak.ts's only same-tree source exerciser (scripts/check-private-leak.ts imports the dist specifier), so mutate=9/testFiles=10 is intentional.

Survey routing predicate, not an independent write or promotion authority. runCheck fails closed (onboarded:false) on every error path -- missing env, ENOENT, malformed YAML, and schema failure all resolve to false, never true. The deciding predicate, publicRepoEntryExists in packages/registry/src/repos-metadata.ts, is not itself in the mutated set, so mutating this wrapper would not exercise the real decision.

Documentation-quality lint for broken relative links. It does not protect a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact; its behavior is adequately covered by conventional tests.

Documentation-quality lint for docs/solutions code examples (parse validity, opt-in symbol/arity checks). It does not protect a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact; its behavior is adequately covered by conventional tests. Whether it belongs in stryker.config.json's mutate set is a separate materiality decision, deliberately left open here.

Supply-chain lint failing on any high or critical advisory that `bun audit --json` reports against the installed dependency tree (see PR #3871). It is a real security-relevant gate, but its rejection paths (fail-closed on empty or unparseable audit output, malformed package entries and advisory records, unrecognized severities, and every high/critical case) are enumerated and asserted directly in scripts/check-override-floors.test.ts. Whether it belongs in stryker.config.json's mutate set is a separate materiality decision, deliberately left open here, matching scripts/check-solutions-examples.ts's precedent.

CI lint that parses allowedVersions values with Renovate's own versioning API (renovate/dist/modules/versioning, util/string-match) and fails on anything Renovate would reject at lookup time. It protects the published default.json preset from a config-breaking edit, not a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact. Every verdict branch (npm range, regex form, rule-declared non-npm versioning, semver fallback, unknown versioning, non-string, templated skip) and the failing rule naming are asserted directly in scripts/check-renovate-ranges.test.ts. Whether it belongs in stryker.config.json's mutate set is a separate materiality decision, deliberately left open here.

Locates, installs and loads the pinned scratch Renovate for the preset gate (pin parsing, prefix resolution, install-command shape, fail-loud version check). CI tooling, not a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact. Pin parsing, prefix resolution, install flags and the missing/mismatched-install failures are asserted in scripts/renovate-runtime.test.ts; the real module loading is exercised by its RENOVATE_PREFIX integration test.

Thin CLI over installRenovate in scripts/renovate-runtime.ts: reads the pin, resolves the prefix, installs, prints the prefix. The logic it delegates to is tested there; this file holds no decision of its own.

CI lint orchestrating renovate-config-validator (--strict --no-global) over default.json, .github/renovate.json5 and the version-pinned github> presets they extend, then the allowedVersions range check. It protects the published default.json preset, not a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact. Fetch retry/404 fall-through, floating/unsupported preset classification, fail-closed fetch errors, and the real validator's exit-code contract are asserted directly in scripts/check-renovate-config.test.ts. Whether it belongs in stryker.config.json's mutate set is a separate materiality decision, deliberately left open here.

Test support: an in-memory Git Data API that the registry writers' tests (merge-back-data, rename-tracked-repo, wiki-repair, wiki-ingest) run against. Fail-closed denylist for learning bodies and log diffs (secret patterns, private repo tokens). It moved from scripts/ unchanged and was outside the mutate list there; its decisions are pinned by decision-table tests in packages/privacy/src/capture-learnings-privacy.test.ts and again through the public-output gate. The public-output gate: one function that blocks any surface body containing a private token, a redacted canonical ID or a secret, and fails closed when the token load failed. Type-only module: it declares the RegistryIo interface (stdout and stderr sinks) and has no runtime code, so there is nothing to mutate.

The pure shape and lookup helpers for metadata/repos.yaml (addRepoEntry, the survey write-back, the rename and visibility lookups). Their rejection paths (RepoEntryNotFoundError, DuplicateRepoIdentityError) are pinned by decision-table tests in repos-metadata.test.ts and exercised through the callers' tests, but the module is not a promotion gate: the data branch, the integrity check and the privacy gates decide what reaches main. It is not in the mutate list because its consumers that are mutated (merge-back-data) do not reach it. Re-evaluate if a mutated gate starts to depend on it.

The App-token writer for metadata/*.yaml on data, with the 409 retry and the branch-protection guard. Its rejection paths (CommitMetadataError codes, CONFLICT_EXHAUSTED) are pinned by commit-metadata.test.ts and every writer's tests exercise it, but it writes only to data, which the repository rulesets and the reconcile integrity check protect, and nothing it returns reaches main without the merge-data privacy gates. It is not in the mutate list because its mutants would score Octokit transport glue and the retry wiring, which core's retry tests already cover. Re-evaluate if it gains a caller outside the data-branch writers.

Scheduled invitation poller: it accepts invitations only from allowlisted inviters and writes new rows to data through commit-metadata. Its decisions (inviter allowlist, privacy refresh, the redacted-ID output, the public-only GITHUB_OUTPUT keys) are pinned by handle-invitation.test.ts. It is not in the mutate list because it is an I/O shell around injected Octokit clients rather than a pure predicate, and the privacy decision it makes (never announce a private repo) is enforced again by gateway-announce and the privacy gates. Re-evaluate if it gains an unattended caller that bypasses them.

Survey write-back: it records a survey outcome on the matching row of metadata/repos.yaml on data. The decisions (name-mismatch, visibility-mismatch, duplicate identity, the exit-0 skip for a missing entry) are pinned by record-survey-result.test.ts, and the write goes through commit-metadata to data only. It is not in the mutate list because it is a thin shell over repos-metadata and commit-metadata, classified separately, and nothing it writes reaches main without the merge-data gates.

Operator recovery tool for survey fields on data, dispatched by hand. Its parsing and failure paths are pinned by reset-survey-status.test.ts, and the write goes through commit-metadata to data only. It is not in the mutate list because it has no unattended caller and its decisions are shared with repos-metadata, classified separately.

Opens or refreshes the data to main promotion PR and files the stale, conflict and journal alerts. The PR it opens is the human-reviewed promotion path: the privacy gates run before it and the conditional auto-merge rule decides what merges. Its decisions are pinned by merge-data-pr.test.ts. It is not in the mutate list because it is an I/O shell around injected Octokit clients, and merge-back-data (mutated) reaches only upsertAlertIssue. Re-evaluate if the PR gains an auto-merge path of its own.

The lookup that stops a rename or merge from stranding a wiki page: findBlockedPublicAssociations, publicAssociationKey and lookupRepoWikiPage, used by reconcile. Its decisions are pinned by metadata-wiki-rename-guard.test.ts and reconcile-wiki-rename-guard.test.ts. It is not in the mutate list because it is consumed only by reconcile, which is not mutated. Re-evaluate together with reconcile.

Refreshes metadata/renovate.yaml on data from the Renovate repos the App installation can see. The sort and dedupe in buildRenovateFile and the 404 handling in discovery are pinned by update-metadata.test.ts. It is not in the mutate list because it is a scheduled writer to data only, behind the same rulesets and gates as the other metadata writers, and it makes no privacy or promotion decision.
